newsitem.title: USA: Hach amends proposal for dual class shrs.
newsitem.headline: Hach amends proposal for dual class shrs.

text.p: Hach Co on Tuesday said its board has approved a modification of the stock dividend it would pay shareholders in conjunction with its plans to implement a dual-class stock structure.

The company said it now plans to pay one Class A common share to shareholders for each common share they currently own. The new Class A shares will be non-voting shares except under limited circumstances, it said.
Under its original plan announced in March, Hach proposed paying a half share each of existing stock and Class A stock for each share held of existing stock, the company said.
The proposed revision will result in the company's stock outstanding doubling to 22.8 million from about 11.4 million shares, with half designated as voting shares, Hach said.
The company said it filed a proxy statement Monday with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Once cleared by the SEC, the statement explaining the revision will be mailed to shareholders, it said.
The proposed dual-class structure and the proposed amendments must be approved by holders of a majority of shares at a meeting scheduled for June 23, the company said.
